study: Konstantopoulos, Li, Miller & van der Ploeg 2016 (EPM) — Indiana mCLASS/Acuity interim-assessment RCT (same experiment as 2013)
eval_evidence: Impact evaluation by IES-funded academic researchers (Konstantopoulos et al., grant R305E090005); program = Indiana DOE statewide interim-assessment rollout using commercial vendor products (Wireless Generation mCLASS, CTB/McGraw-Hill Acuity). Evaluators independent of the vendors.
developer_evidence: Training was the vendor/state 'training associated with each product' delivered through Indiana's statewide rollout, not by the impact-evaluation research team. Control schools lacked 'access to these assessments and their associated trainings.'
cascade_evidence: Statewide vendor/state training of users is described, but the paper does not specify whether classroom teachers were trained directly or via a district/lead-trainer cascade. Silent on transmission hops.
counterfactual_evidence: Control schools 'did not receive access to these assessments and their associated trainings, and operated under business-as-usual conditions.' True BAU.
coaching_evidence: Intervention = interim-assessment system plus associated vendor training; the publication describes 'reports on test outcomes and training' but does not detail PD format/intensity or any ongoing in-class coaching. Silent on coaching.
student_dose_evidence: Students take the interim/diagnostic assessments directly (mCLASS face-to-face probes; Acuity online tests within a class period), but these are diagnostic assessments feeding the teacher's regular instruction, not an added tutoring/pull-out/extra-instruction dose.
maturity_evidence: Same 2009-2010 RCT as the 2013 paper; treatment year was the first implementation year for volunteer schools. The paper notes only 10 of ~70 schools had used a vendor product the prior year, so the large majority were first-year.
